title: The Shapes of Talk
corpus_scope: 199,031 review threads, 2018–2026 · pure reply structure, no machine reading anywhere
question: Does the reviewer ever come back after the authors respond, and how has that reply structure changed over nine years?

figures.title: A census of skeletons: what became of each year's review threads
figures.deck: Reviewers came back to 43.8% of threads in 2025 but only 17.7% in 2026.

claims.statement: Reviewers came back to 43.8% of threads in 2025 but only 17.7% in 2026.
Stumps grew from 9% in 2021 to 26% — one review thread in four now ends in silence before it begins.
claims.derivation: shapes['2021'].stump / total 2021 threads = 8.7%, ≈9%; shapes['2026'].stump / total 2026 threads = 26.4%, ≈26%

figures.title: Five real skeletons, pressed like botanical specimens
figures.deck: Five real discussions pressed flat: long vines of exchange beside silent stumps.

claims.statement: In 2026, threads where the reviewer returned were accepted at 50–51% against 39% for monologues and 1.2% for stumps.

caveats.text: Each year's discussion rules differ — response windows, mandatory acknowledgements — so the year-to-year levels track the venue's process as well as its people.
Read the acceptance-rate direction both ways, since authors triage which battles to fight and which papers to quietly abandon.
